born.why: The code improves survival by prioritizing emergency eating when hunger is critical, distinguishing between known safe/poison species and using trait overlap analysis for unknown fruits to avoid probable poisons while allowing exploration when hungry.

The code implements a risk-based learning strategy: it avoids known poisonous traits, carries safe species, tastes uncertain ones when hungry to gain data, and prioritizes survival by eating immediately only when near starvation.

The code prioritizes safety by tasting unknown fruits unless starving, leveraging past diary entries to avoid poisonous species while seeking sustenance, ensuring long-term survival through cautious exploration and efficient consumption of known safe foods.

The code prioritizes safety by always tasting unknown fruits to build a reliable diary of safe/poisonous species, only eating known safe fruits or starving critically, thereby minimizing death risk while maximizing long-term caloric efficiency.

This code improves safety by strictly avoiding known poisonous fruits, using smell heuristics to prioritize safe-eating of promising fruits while cautiously tasting risky ones only when hunger allows for some risk, and managing inventory via pantry checks to avoid unnecessary foraging when stocked.

The code prioritizes starvation survival, then uses a scoring system based on shared traits (smell/shape/color) to estimate safety of unknown fruits. It distinguishes between "known safe" (carry if not hungry, eat if hungry), "known bad" (leave), and "unknown" (taste if hungry enough to justify potential risk, otherwise leave). It avoids over-relying on single trait matches by requiring multiple matches for high confidence in safety.

The code prioritizes survival by eating when starving, avoids known poisonous fruits via diary lookup, and uses similarity matching to safely try new fruits of the same appearance as previously safe ones, otherwise tasting cautiously or leaving.

The code improves by using trait similarity (color/shape) from the diary to infer safety for unknown fruits, allowing safe "eating" when similar known-safe fruits are prevalent, while retaining robust handling of known safe/poisonous fruits and extreme starvation risks.

The code prioritizes survival by eating immediately when hunger is critical, avoids confirmed poison, carries known safe food to reduce future foraging effort, and cautiously tastes new species only when hunger is low enough to mitigate the risk of potential harm.
